source_text:
Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

Hearing screening indicates bilateral hearing loss. Formal audiometry was completed this week, and the signed audiologist report states that mean unaided threshold in the better ear was 47 dB, averaged over 500, 1000, 2000 and 3000 Hz. The report explicitly confirms removal of both hearing aids during testing and identifies the better ear, so those measurements are distinguished from the driver's account of hearing reasonably well when his aids are working.

One aid intermittently stops working near the end of a shift, and the driver sometimes misses dispatch instructions in background noise; no current aided-performance assessment establishes whether the aids meet the relevant standard. He brings a repair booking, which the nurse does not treat as evidence that the fault has been corrected.

He also describes variable home pressure readings, but today's BP 158/94 mmHg is a single seated observation and no clinician has documented a persistent current pressure. The nurse retains the verified unaided audiometry without converting either the pending aid repair or the incomplete blood-pressure history into a confirmed result.
